destinations.name: Türkiye
destinations.tagline: Quality education between Europe and Asia, with affordable fees and strong scholarships.
destinations.intro: Türkiye combines a long academic tradition with modern campuses, a welcoming culture and comparatively affordable costs. Cities such as Istanbul, Ankara and Izmir are home to public and private universities that teach many programs in English, and the country is a natural bridge between Europe and Asia.
destinations.system: Higher education is overseen by the Council of Higher Education (YÖK). Bachelor's degrees usually take four years, with longer programs in fields such as medicine, dentistry and architecture. Master's degrees take one to two years, and PhDs three to five. Universities are either state (public) or foundation (private) institutions.
requirements: Secondary school or bachelor's certificate and transcripts
Proof of English (IELTS, TOEFL or university test) for English programs
Turkish proficiency or a preparatory year for Turkish-taught programs
Some universities require their own entrance exam or the YÖS
destinations.tuition: State universities generally charge modest tuition for international students. Foundation (private) universities charge higher fees, but many offer merit-based discounts. Living costs are lower than in most of Western Europe, especially outside Istanbul.

scholarships.title: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları)
scholarships.desc: Government scholarship covering tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation, health insurance and a Turkish language year.

scholarships.title: University merit discounts
scholarships.desc: Many foundation universities offer partial or full tuition discounts based on academic results.

process: Prepare documents and English or Turkish test results
Apply directly to universities or through Türkiye Scholarships
Travel and apply for a residence permit after arrival
destinations.visa: Students apply for a student visa at the Turkish embassy or consulate using their university acceptance letter. After arrival, students must apply for a student residence permit (ikamet) within the required period. We guide you through both steps.

faqs.q: Can I study in Türkiye in English?
faqs.a: Yes. Many universities offer English-taught bachelor's and master's programs.

faqs.q: Can I work while studying in Türkiye?
faqs.a: Work rules for international students are limited and depend on your program level and permits. We explain the current rules during counseling.

faqs.q: Is Türkiye safe for international students?
faqs.a: Türkiye hosts large numbers of international students, and major university cities are generally welcoming. We share practical safety advice before you travel.

destinations.name: United Kingdom
destinations.tagline: World-renowned universities and shorter degrees that save time and cost.
destinations.intro: The United Kingdom is home to some of the world's oldest and most respected universities. Degrees are shorter than in many countries, with most master's programs completed in a single year, and the UK offers a post-study work route for eligible graduates.
destinations.system: Undergraduate degrees usually take three years in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and four in Scotland. Most taught master's degrees take one year, and PhDs three to four years. Undergraduate applications are made through UCAS, while postgraduate applications go directly to universities.
requirements: English test score, usually IELTS for UKVI, or an accepted alternative
destinations.tuition: Tuition for international students varies by university, subject and level, with laboratory and clinical subjects usually costing more. Living costs are highest in London. We give you current fee ranges for the universities on your shortlist.

scholarships.title: Chevening Scholarships
scholarships.desc: UK government scholarships for one-year master's degrees, for future leaders.

scholarships.title: Commonwealth Scholarships
scholarships.desc: Scholarships for students from Commonwealth countries, including Pakistan.

scholarships.title: University scholarships
scholarships.desc: Many UK universities offer international merit scholarships and tuition discounts.

process: Prepare your statement, references and English test
Apply through UCAS or directly to universities
Accept your offer and pay any deposit
Receive your CAS from the university
destinations.visa: International students apply for the UK Student visa using a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from their university. You must show you can pay tuition and living costs, meet the English requirement, and pay the Immigration Health Surcharge. We guide you through the financial evidence carefully, as it is a common reason for refusal.

faqs.q: Can I work while studying in the UK?
faqs.a: Student visa holders on degree programs can usually work part-time during term and full-time during official vacations, within the visa conditions.

faqs.q: Is there a post-study work option?
faqs.a: Yes. Eligible graduates can apply for the Graduate route after completing their degree. We explain the current rules and duration.

faqs.q: Do I need IELTS for the UK?
faqs.a: Many universities require IELTS for UKVI or another approved test, though some accept alternatives. We check your universities' requirements.

destinations.name: Germany
destinations.tagline: Tuition-free public universities and a powerful engineering tradition.
card_points: Low or no tuition at public universities
destinations.intro: Germany is one of the most popular destinations for international students, thanks to high academic standards and public universities that charge little or no tuition for most programs. It is especially strong in engineering, technology and the sciences.
destinations.system: German higher education includes research universities (Universitäten) and universities of applied sciences (Fachhochschulen) with a practical focus. Bachelor's degrees take three to four years and master's degrees two years. Some bachelor's applicants need a preparatory course (Studienkolleg) before starting.
requirements: Proof of English or German depending on the program language
Some programs require a minimum grade or an aptitude test
destinations.tuition: Most public universities charge no tuition for most programs, though students pay a semester contribution. Some states, such as Baden-Württemberg, charge tuition for non-EU students. Students must show sufficient funds for living costs, usually through a blocked account.

scholarships.title: DAAD Scholarships
scholarships.desc: Germany's academic exchange service offers scholarships for master's and doctoral students.

scholarships.title: Deutschlandstipendium
scholarships.desc: Merit-based scholarships offered through German universities.

scholarships.title: Foundation scholarships
scholarships.desc: Political and private foundations offer scholarships for strong candidates.

process: Check the recognition of your qualifications
Open a blocked account and arrange health insurance
Apply for your national student visa
destinations.visa: Students apply for a German national visa for study at the German embassy or through its appointed visa service. You will need your admission letter, proof of funds (usually a blocked account), health insurance and academic documents. Appointment waiting times can be long, so we help you plan ahead.

faqs.q: Is studying in Germany really free?
faqs.a: Most public universities charge no tuition, but you pay a semester contribution and must cover your living costs.

faqs.q: Do I need to speak German?
faqs.a: Not for English-taught programs, but basic German helps a lot with daily life and part-time work.

faqs.q: What is a blocked account?
faqs.a: A special bank account showing you have funds for living costs. You can withdraw a fixed amount each month after arrival.

destinations.name: Italy
destinations.tagline: Historic universities, income-based fees and generous regional scholarships.
destinations.intro: Italy offers historic universities, a rich culture and some of the most affordable quality education in Europe. Public universities set fees according to family income, and regional scholarships can cover tuition, accommodation and meals for eligible students.
destinations.system: Italy follows the European system: a three-year bachelor's degree (laurea), a two-year master's degree (laurea magistrale), and single-cycle degrees of five to six years for fields such as medicine and law. Many universities offer English-taught programs, especially at master's level.
requirements: Entrance tests for some programs such as medicine
destinations.tuition: Public universities charge fees based on family income and assets, which makes them very affordable for many students. Private universities charge higher fixed fees. Living costs vary by city, with Milan and Rome among the most expensive.

scholarships.title: Regional DSU scholarships
scholarships.desc: Regional scholarships based on financial need, which may cover fees, accommodation and meals.

scholarships.title: Italian government scholarships
scholarships.desc: Scholarships offered by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs for international students.

scholarships.title: University scholarships
scholarships.desc: Merit-based awards and fee waivers offered by individual universities.

process: Apply to universities and receive pre-acceptance
Apply for regional scholarships where eligible
Request your residence permit after arrival
destinations.visa: Students need a national (type D) study visa from the Italian embassy or its appointed visa service. Requirements include pre-enrollment confirmation, proof of funds, accommodation and health insurance. After arrival, you must apply for a residence permit for study.

faqs.q: Can I study medicine in English in Italy?
faqs.a: Yes. Several public universities offer English-taught medicine programs, with admission through an entrance test.

faqs.q: Are scholarships based on merit or need?
faqs.a: Regional DSU scholarships are mainly need-based, while university awards are often merit-based.

destinations.name: Spain
destinations.tagline: A vibrant lifestyle, respected business schools and a global language.
destinations.intro: Spain offers respected public universities, well-known business schools and an excellent quality of life. Studying in Spain also gives you the chance to learn Spanish, one of the world's most widely spoken languages.
destinations.system: Bachelor's degrees (grado) usually take four years and official master's degrees one to two years. Many public universities teach mainly in Spanish, while English-taught programs are growing, especially in business and at private institutions.
requirements: Spanish or English proficiency depending on the program
destinations.tuition: Public university fees are set by each region and are generally moderate. Private universities and business schools charge higher fees. Living costs are lower than in many other Western European countries, especially outside Madrid and Barcelona.

scholarships.title: University scholarships
scholarships.desc: Merit and need-based awards offered by Spanish universities and business schools.

scholarships.title: Erasmus+ programs
scholarships.desc: Joint master's programs with scholarships through the European Union.

process: Shortlist programs and check language requirements
Obtain your student residence card after arrival
destinations.visa: Students apply for a Spanish student visa at the embassy or its appointed visa service, with their admission letter, proof of funds, health insurance and other documents. After arrival, students obtain a foreigner identity card (TIE) for the length of their studies.

faqs.q: Do I need to speak Spanish?
faqs.a: Not for English-taught programs, but Spanish helps with daily life and many programs are taught only in Spanish.

faqs.q: Can I work while studying in Spain?
faqs.a: Students can usually work part-time within limits set by the immigration rules. We explain the current conditions.

destinations.name: France
destinations.tagline: Prestigious grandes écoles, public universities and the Eiffel scholarship.
destinations.intro: France is known for its public universities, prestigious grandes écoles and world-class business schools. It offers a wide range of English-taught master's programs and a strong research tradition.
destinations.system: France follows the LMD system: licence (bachelor's, three years), master (two years) and doctorat (three years). Alongside public universities, grandes écoles offer selective programs in engineering, business and public administration.
requirements: Applications through the Campus France procedure for many applicants
destinations.tuition: Public universities charge regulated fees for international students, which are still lower than in many countries. Grandes écoles and business schools charge considerably higher fees. Paris is the most expensive city to live in.

scholarships.title: Eiffel Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.desc: French government scholarship for outstanding international master's and PhD students.

scholarships.title: Institution scholarships
scholarships.desc: Many universities and grandes écoles offer fee waivers and merit scholarships.

process: Create your Campus France account if required
Apply for your long-stay student visa
destinations.visa: Students apply for a long-stay student visa (VLS-TS) after completing any required Campus France steps. You must show admission, sufficient funds and accommodation. The visa must be validated online after arrival in France.

faqs.q: Can I study in France in English?
faqs.a: Yes. Many master's programs and business school programs are taught in English.

faqs.q: What is Campus France?
faqs.a: Campus France is the French agency that manages the application and pre-visa procedure for international students in many countries.

destinations.name: Hungary
destinations.tagline: Respected medical schools, low costs and the Stipendium Hungaricum.
destinations.intro: Hungary is a well-established destination for international students, especially in medicine, dentistry and engineering. Its universities offer many English-taught programs, living costs are moderate, and the Stipendium Hungaricum scholarship is open to students from Pakistan.
destinations.system: Hungary follows the European system of bachelor's (three to four years), master's (one to two years) and doctoral degrees. Medicine, dentistry and pharmacy are single long-cycle programs of five to six years.
destinations.tuition: Tuition is moderate for most programs, with medical programs costing more. Living costs are lower than in Western Europe, including in Budapest.

scholarships.title: Stipendium Hungaricum
scholarships.desc: Hungarian government scholarship covering tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation support and health insurance, for students from partner countries including Pakistan.

process: Apply directly or through Stipendium Hungaricum
Take any entrance exams or interviews
Apply for your residence permit for study
destinations.visa: Students apply for a residence permit for study purposes, usually with an entry visa, using their university acceptance letter, proof of funds, accommodation and health insurance. We guide you through the current procedure.

faqs.q: Is the Stipendium Hungaricum open to Pakistani students?
faqs.a: Yes. Pakistan is among the partner countries. Applicants must also be nominated by the sending authority in Pakistan.

faqs.q: Are Hungarian medical degrees recognized?
faqs.a: Hungarian medical degrees are recognized across the European Union. Recognition elsewhere depends on the local medical council.

destinations.name: Poland
destinations.tagline: Affordable European education in a fast-growing economy.
destinations.intro: Poland offers recognized European degrees at affordable prices, a growing economy and modern cities such as Warsaw, Kraków and Wrocław. Its universities offer a wide range of English-taught programs.
destinations.system: Poland follows the European system: bachelor's degrees take three to four years, master's degrees one and a half to two years, and long-cycle programs such as medicine around six years.
requirements: Entrance exams or interviews for some programs
destinations.tuition: Tuition is affordable compared with Western Europe, with medical programs costing more. Living costs are moderate, with Warsaw being the most expensive city.

scholarships.title: NAWA programs
scholarships.desc: The Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange offers scholarships for international students and researchers.

scholarships.title: University scholarships
scholarships.desc: Some universities offer fee reductions for high-achieving students.

process: Pay the first tuition installment if required
Apply for your national student visa
destinations.visa: Students apply for a Polish national (type D) visa for study at the embassy or its appointed visa service. You will need your acceptance letter, proof of tuition payment where required, proof of funds and health insurance.

faqs.q: Is Poland part of the Schengen area?
faqs.a: Yes. A Polish national visa or residence permit allows travel within the Schengen area under its rules.

faqs.q: Are programs available in English?
faqs.a: Yes. Polish universities offer many English-taught bachelor's and master's programs.

destinations.name: Malaysia
destinations.tagline: International branch campuses and affordable living in a Muslim-friendly country.
destinations.intro: Malaysia is a popular choice for students from Pakistan, offering English-taught programs, international branch campuses of well-known universities, and a familiar, Muslim-friendly environment at an affordable cost.
destinations.system: Bachelor's degrees usually take three to four years, often after a foundation year. Master's degrees take one to two years. Malaysia's higher education includes public universities, private universities and branch campuses of foreign universities.
requirements: English proficiency, often IELTS or equivalent
A foundation year for some undergraduate programs
destinations.tuition: Tuition is generally affordable, especially compared with the UK or Australia, while branch campuses can award degrees from their home universities. Living costs are moderate.

scholarships.title: University scholarships
scholarships.desc: Many Malaysian and branch campus universities offer merit-based scholarships and tuition discounts.

process: The university applies for your student pass through EMGS
Travel and complete the student pass process
destinations.visa: International students in Malaysia receive a student pass. The application is usually submitted by your university through Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS), and includes a medical check. We guide you through the documents and timeline.

faqs.q: Can I earn a foreign degree in Malaysia?
faqs.a: Yes. Branch campuses award degrees from their home universities in the UK, Australia and elsewhere.

faqs.q: Is Malaysia affordable for students?
faqs.a: Yes. Tuition and living costs are generally lower than in many Western destinations.

destinations.name: China
destinations.tagline: Fast-rising universities, strong scholarships and English-taught MBBS programs.
destinations.intro: China's leading universities have risen quickly in global rankings and attract large numbers of international students. Strong government scholarships and English-taught programs, including medicine, make China a popular choice for students from Pakistan.
destinations.system: Bachelor's degrees usually take four years, and five to six years for medicine. Master's degrees take two to three years and doctorates three to four. Programs are offered in Chinese and, increasingly, in English.
requirements: English or Chinese (HSK) proficiency depending on the program
Study plan or research proposal for postgraduate study
destinations.tuition: Tuition is moderate and varies by university and program. Living costs are lower than in most Western destinations, though major cities cost more.

scholarships.title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC)
scholarships.desc: Scholarships covering tuition, accommodation, a stipend and medical insurance.

scholarships.title: University and provincial scholarships
scholarships.desc: Many universities and provinces offer their own scholarships for international students.

process: Prepare documents and the physical examination form
Apply to universities and scholarship programs
Receive your admission letter and JW201/JW202 form
destinations.visa: Long-term students apply for an X1 student visa using their admission letter and the JW201 or JW202 form, then convert it to a residence permit after arrival. Short-term students use an X2 visa.

faqs.q: Are Chinese MBBS degrees recognized in Pakistan?
faqs.a: Graduates must meet the requirements of the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council. Choose a university and program that is recognized. We check this for you.

faqs.q: Do I need to learn Chinese?
faqs.a: Not for English-taught programs, though basic Chinese is very useful in daily life and clinical training.

destinations.name: Australia
destinations.tagline: High-ranking universities, a great lifestyle and post-study work options.
destinations.intro: Australia is known for high-ranking universities, a safe and multicultural society and an excellent quality of life. International students can work part-time during their studies, and eligible graduates may access post-study work options.
destinations.system: Bachelor's degrees usually take three years, with an optional honours year. Master's degrees take one to two years. All courses offered to international students must be registered on CRICOS.
requirements: English test such as IELTS or PTE
Evidence that you are a genuine student
destinations.tuition: Tuition varies widely by university and course, and living costs in major cities are relatively high. Students must show sufficient funds for the visa. We provide current figures for your shortlist.

scholarships.title: Australia Awards
scholarships.desc: Australian government scholarships for students from eligible countries.

scholarships.title: University scholarships
scholarships.desc: Most Australian universities offer international merit scholarships and tuition reductions.

process: Accept the offer and pay the deposit
destinations.visa: International students apply for the Student visa (subclass 500) using their Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE). You must show you are a genuine student, have enough funds, meet English requirements and hold Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC).

faqs.q: Can I work while studying in Australia?
faqs.a: Yes. Student visa holders can work within the limits set by their visa conditions, which allow more hours during holidays.

faqs.q: What is the Genuine Student requirement?
faqs.a: It assesses whether you genuinely intend to study in Australia. A clear, honest statement and consistent documents are essential.

destinations.name: Canada
destinations.tagline: Welcoming, high-quality education with pathways after graduation.
destinations.intro: Canada offers respected universities and colleges, a welcoming multicultural society and co-op programs that combine study with work experience. Eligible graduates may apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit.
destinations.system: Universities offer bachelor's degrees (usually four years), master's and doctoral degrees. Colleges offer diplomas, certificates and applied degrees, often with co-op placements. Students must enrol at a Designated Learning Institution (DLI).
requirements: English test such as IELTS or an accepted alternative
Letters of recommendation for postgraduate study
A Provincial or Territorial Attestation Letter for most study permit applicants
destinations.tuition: Tuition varies by province, institution and program, with colleges generally charging less than universities. Students must show proof of funds for tuition and living costs when applying for a study permit.

scholarships.title: University entrance scholarships
scholarships.desc: Many Canadian universities offer automatic and merit-based entrance scholarships.

scholarships.title: Graduate funding
scholarships.desc: Research master's and PhD students often receive funding through assistantships.

process: Apply and receive your letter of acceptance
Obtain your Provincial or Territorial Attestation Letter if required
destinations.visa: Most international students need a study permit, applied for online with a letter of acceptance from a DLI, proof of funds and, in most cases, a Provincial or Territorial Attestation Letter. Canadian study permit rules have changed frequently, so we check the latest requirements for every application.

faqs.q: Can I work while studying in Canada?
faqs.a: Many study permit holders can work off-campus within set limits. Check the current conditions on your permit.

faqs.q: Are college programs eligible for a work permit after graduation?
faqs.a: Some are, depending on the program and current rules. We check eligibility before you apply.

destinations.name: United States
destinations.tagline: The world's largest choice of universities and flexible degree programs.
destinations.intro: The United States has the largest and most diverse higher education system in the world, from research universities to liberal arts and community colleges. Programs are flexible, and eligible graduates can gain work experience through Optional Practical Training (OPT).
destinations.system: Bachelor's degrees usually take four years and allow students to explore subjects before choosing a major. Community colleges offer two-year associate degrees that can transfer to universities. Master's degrees take one to two years and PhDs four to six.
programs: STEM programs with extended OPT eligibility
requirements: English test such as TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo
SAT, GRE or GMAT for some programs
destinations.tuition: Tuition varies widely between public and private institutions and between states. Community colleges are the most affordable route. Many universities offer substantial financial aid and assistantships.

scholarships.title: Fulbright Program
scholarships.desc: U.S. government scholarships for graduate study, administered in Pakistan by USEFP.

scholarships.title: University aid and assistantships
scholarships.desc: Merit scholarships, need-based aid, and teaching or research assistantships for graduate students.

process: Receive admission and your Form I-20
Pay the SEVIS fee and complete the DS-160
destinations.visa: Students apply for an F-1 visa using the Form I-20 issued by their university. You must pay the SEVIS fee, complete the DS-160 form and attend an interview at the U.S. Embassy or Consulate. Clear funding evidence and strong, honest answers are essential.

faqs.q: Is a visa interview required?
faqs.a: Most F-1 applicants attend an interview. We prepare you with mock interviews based on your own case.

faqs.q: What is OPT?
faqs.a: Optional Practical Training lets eligible F-1 students work in their field after graduation, with an extension for eligible STEM graduates.
